'''US Mobile''' is an American [[mobile virtual network operator]] (MVNO) that uses the [[T-Mobile US|T-Mobile]], [[Verizon Wireless]], and [[AT&T Mobility|AT&T]] networks (branded as "Light Speed", "Warp", and "Dark Star" respectively) to provide [[cell network|cellular]] services to their customers.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Villas-Boas |first=Antonio |date=February 27, 2025 |title=US Mobile review: Exceptionally cheap and flexible phone plans |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/guides/tech/us-mobile-review |url-status=live |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/pIclc |archive-date=February 22, 2026 |work=[[Business Insider]] |language=en |no-pp=y}}</ref>

Services offered by US Mobile do not involve long term contracts and are structured to allow periodic changes by the user. The carrier does not use network operator names in its marketing and offers Verizon coverage under the brand "Warp" (formerly "Super LTE"), T-Mobile service under the brand "Light Speed" (previously "GSM 5G" and "GSM LTE") and the AT&T network, branded as "Dark Star".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Will US Mobile succeed where Google Fi Failed? |url=https://www.lightreading.com/mobile-core/will-us-mobile-succeed-where-google-fi-failed- |access-date=August 7, 2024 |website=LightReading |language=en}}</ref> Similar to other prepaid carriers, the provider also sells phones through its website and partners with third parties and various retailers for distribution.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Exclusive: US Mobile Is the First Legit Xiaomi, Meizu Carrier in U.S.|url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/exclusive-us-mobile-is-the-first-legit-xiaomi-meizu-carrier-in-us|access-date=August 14, 2021|website=PCMAG|date=February 2016 |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=July 26, 2021 |title=US Mobile secures $11.5M in funding, eSIM and retail coming |url=https://www.fiercewireless.com/operators/us-mobile-secures-11-5m-funding-esim-and-retail-coming |access-date=August 14, 2021 |website=FierceWireless |language=en}}</ref>

== History ==
Based in [[New York, New York|New York City]], US Mobile was founded in 2015 by [[chief executive officer|CEO]] Ahmed Khattak as a [[GSM]]-based service provider.<ref>{{Cite web|title=US Mobile launches service on 'nation's biggest LTE network' as it introduces iPhone X promo|url=https://www.fiercewireless.com/wireless/us-mobile-launches-service-nation-s-biggest-lte-network-as-it-intros-iphone-x-promo|access-date=August 14, 2021|website=FierceWireless|date=October 30, 2017 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=CreativityTurf|date=December 4, 2012|title=Ahmed Khattak : Built a $35 Million Company and Growing, Selling Unlocked Phones and Mobile Devices|url=https://creativityturf.wordpress.com/2012/12/04/ahmed-khattak-built-a-35-million-company-and-growing-selling-unlocked-phones-and-mobile-devices/|access-date=January 1, 2022|website=CreativityTurf|language=en}}</ref>

In 2020, the company claimed to have around 250,000 customers.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Verizon's Visible gears up for eSIM support|url=https://www.fiercewireless.com/operators/verizon-s-visible-gears-up-for-esim-support|access-date=August 14, 2021|website=FierceWireless|date=October 12, 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

In 2021, it was announced that the carrier would offer pooled plans where customers pay for data in bulk to use across multiple devices and users.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Chernova|first=Yuliya|date=July 20, 2021|title=US Mobile Sees Data Pools as Key to Monetizing 5G|language=en-US|work=Wall Street Journal|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/us-mobile-sees-data-pools-as-key-to-monetizing-5g-11626778800|access-date=August 14, 2021|issn=0099-9660}}</ref> The pooled plan service saw usage from 300 to 3,000 lines in one month, according to the company's CEO.<ref name=":0" /> That same year, the company raised $11.5 million in [[Series A round|Series A]] funding from Volition Capital.<ref>{{Cite web|last=FinSMEs|date=July 22, 2021|title=US Mobile Raises $11.5M in Series A Funding|url=https://www.finsmes.com/2021/07/us-mobile-raises-11-5m-in-series-a-funding.html|access-date=August 14, 2021|website=FinSMEs|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2022, it was reported that the company launched [[5G]] C-Band access on its network, adding onto the existing 5G UW mmWave access from Verizon.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Visible, US Mobile Also Get Verizon's New 5G System|url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/visible-us-mobile-also-get-verizons-new-5g-system|access-date=January 10, 2022|website=PCMAG|date=January 5, 2022 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Verizon Details C-Band 5G Launch Date, Pricing, Where You Can Get It|url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/verizon-details-c-band-5g-launch-date-pricing-where-you-can-get-it|access-date=January 10, 2022|website=PCMAG|date=January 4, 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

In late 2023, the company announced it would begin offering customers the option to activate service on [[AT&T]]’s network, referred to internally as "Dark Star." The option became available on July 15, 2024, with full support beginning two weeks later. With service available on the three major U.S. wireless telecoms, the company began referring to itself as a "Super Carrier".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Grush |first=Andrew |date=August 26, 2024 |title=Verizon vs US Mobile: Big Red versus the so-called Super Carrier |url=https://www.androidauthority.com/verizon-vs-us-mobile-3474755/ |access-date=September 9, 2024 |website=Android Authority |language=en}}</ref>
